raw.assessment: The incumbent provides a repeatable conversational routine and printed access: seven frequent attendees value its structure (H3-O6), and nine regularly rely on print (H3-O7). Predictability reducing entry and coordination effort is a plausible account, not an established cause. Its concrete limitation is that five occasional attendees struggled to enter conversations already familiar to partners (H3-O6); the same continuity may benefit regulars while requiring an entry bridge for others. Pair delays and changes (H3-O5) do not establish proficiency mismatch. Only 49 of 72 slips report the speaking target and 48 identify preparation; missing slips, untimed speech and unlinked weeks prevent an all-attendee success estimate. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Retaining the routine while testing narrow changes is warranted.

openings.claim: Explicit session dates and one clearly marked next preparation task on each printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier tasks.
openings.delta: Retain the weekly topic and optional message, but add a reusable dated preparation box, available at each session regardless of previous attendance.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline and correct next-task identification rises; blank answers may persist if access or comprehension dominates.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, count correct, earlier and blank preparation answers against total attendance; separately log printing and clarification minutes. Seek 85% correct with total coordination below 90 minutes weekly.
assumptions: Volunteers can specify the next task before printing.
Printed information remains obtainable without an account or smartphone.

openings.claim: A shared fresh opening prompt with a brief reciprocal introduction may help occasional attendees enter conversations without discarding the familiar session structure.
openings.delta: Replace the first pair prompt with a self-contained exchange requiring no previous-session knowledge; partners choose follow-up complexity without public proficiency labels.
openings.prediction: Early partner changes and reported entry difficulty decrease, especially among occasional attendees; unchanged pair-formation delays would locate a separate bottleneck.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary and fresh opening prompts across six sessions. Observe formation delay and early changes; ask anonymous attendance-frequency, entry-difficulty and useful-speaking questions. Record coordination time and preserve the 75-minute session.
assumptions: Fresh prompts can be drawn from existing sheets.
Changing attendance composition limits causal interpretation.

raw.assessment: Reported practice and preparation fall below targets among returned slips, but 72 slips cover 97 attendances and speaking time was not measured. Attendance continuity, pairing delays and task confusion suggest testable possibilities, not established causes. Both proposals are hypotheses requiring six-session outcome and workload checks.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: give each partner different information about a fresh, self-contained everyday scenario so even a newcomer has something their partner needs to learn.
openings.delta: Preserve the familiar session structure while replacing shared conversational history with reciprocal information gaps. Offer optional sentence starters without proficiency labels; use four six-minute exchanges with alternating lead roles and one optional partner change.
openings.prediction: Occasional attendees report easier entry and more useful practice; speaking becomes less concentrated within pairs. Allocated lead time alone does not establish useful speaking time.
openings.probe: Compare matched shared-sheet and split-information rounds, reversing order across sessions. Anonymously observe actual speech distribution; collect usefulness and entry-difficulty reports with optional recent-attendance counts. Track preparation and printing time against the weekly cap.
assumptions: Reusable split-information sheets can be prepared within unpaid volunteer capacity.
Information asymmetry stimulates conversation at differing levels without becoming a reading exercise.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: use one enduring preparation mission: bring one real question you want to ask in the language. Learner questions become the next session's conversational material.
openings.delta: Replace changing topic-dependent homework with a stable, meaningful action printed on every sheet and available on paper at the venue. Anyone arriving unprepared can choose a question from existing prompts, preserving access after absences.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task errors and preparation clarification messages decline while prepared questions generate useful conversation. Topic-selection effort decreases sufficiently to offset question support.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, ask every attendee to name the next preparation action without viewing the sheet; record whether brought questions actually support useful speaking. Log coordination activities separately and audit paper access for absent participants. Assess the original 80%, 85% and under-90-minute targets.
assumptions: The venue permits dependable paper pickup between sessions.
A repeated mission remains useful across levels and does not narrow conversational variety.

openings.claim: Date sheets and clearly mark one next preparation task.
openings.discriminator: Earlier-task errors decline; blanks may persist.
openings.probe: Count correct/earlier/blank answers against attendance; log printing and clarification minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Requires advance task selection and dependable paper access.

openings.claim: Keep the familiar routine; start pairs with a fresh self-contained reciprocal introduction and optional follow-up complexity.
openings.discriminator: Entry difficulty and early changes decrease; formation delays may persist independently.
openings.fit: Preserves H3-C1–C4; no public level labels.
openings.probe: Alternate ordinary/fresh prompts; observe delays/changes and anonymously ask attendance frequency, entry difficulty and useful speaking.
openings.uncertainty: Changing attendance confounds comparisons; existing sheets must supply prompts.

openings.claim: Give partners complementary scenario information, optional sentence starters, four six-minute exchanges, alternating leads and one optional partner change.
openings.discriminator: Reciprocal information needs improve entry and speech distribution beyond shared fresh prompts.
openings.probe: Compare shared/split-information rounds, reverse order, observe speech distribution and collect entry/usefulness reports.
openings.uncertainty: Allocated time is not useful speech; reading and sheet-production burden may dominate.

openings.claim: Replace changing homework with one enduring mission: bring a real question; offer existing prompts to unprepared arrivals.
openings.discriminator: Stable preparation reduces confusion and topic-selection effort while generating conversation.
openings.probe: Ask next action without sheets; check question usefulness, coordination activities and absent-participant paper access.
openings.uncertainty: Pickup permission, support workload and continued variety remain unverified.

lineage.reason: Adds information asymmetry and turn structure.

post_distill.decision: Test separately over six sessions against original 80% speaking, 85% preparation and weekly coordination below 90 minutes, within 75-minute sessions. All remain hypotheses: 72 slips cover 97 attendances, speech was untimed and weeks unlinked; proficiency mismatch is unestablished.
